roundShape: Narrow round, as the architect asked: 72a07b49 changes two test rigs and one product line (refreshHeldClaims). Round 17's behaviour evidence stands.

implementerProof.how: Re-ran the implementer's command myself: both tests pass 50 of 50 with -race (GOMAXPROCS=4) and 50 of 50 without it.

failures.criterion: The pull request merges into main (the architect's standing instruction: complete failing on a conflict).
failures.evidence: gh pr view 2406 reads CONFLICTING / DIRTY at 0433444e, against main faf3e74d. Main changed three files the PR also changes: packages/envoy/AGENTS.md and packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/README.md (#2422, 8a72cf79, lays both out one sentence per line) and packages/envoy/cmd/listener/api_test.go (#2517, e018f1d3). All three are docs or a test, so the forward merge may be a confirmation round if it resolves them as text. GitHub ran no CI on 72a07b49.

proof.criterion: The refreshHeldClaims change: a refresh that loses to a newer claim keeps the newer one, and a sweep cannot take a live claim with or without the change.
proof.surface: internal/dispatch/api against Postgres 16, through a test added with go -overlay, so the workspace is not changed
proof.command: go test -overlay ov/race-head.json -run '^TestARefreshThatLosesToAKeyedRepeatKeepsTheRepeatsClaim$' -count=3; the same with ov/race-old.json, which restores the old condition `if _, waiting := m.claims[claim.key]; waiting`
proof.observed: The test lets the refresh's statement commit, then writes a newer claim to the row and the map (what queueLocked records for a keyed repeat), and then lets the refresh record its result. At head the sender keeps the newer claim, the next refresh moves the row on, and the attempt is sent once: 3 of 3 pass. Reading the code: no path reaches that gap today, because a keyed repeat claims only a free attempt (comment_mention_sender.go:476-478, DeliveryClaimFreeSQL) and a refresh that committed has just made the row live. The sweep takes only lapsed rows, and the row's claim only moves forward under either version, so neither lets the sweep take a live claim. The new condition matters only if the map and the row could disagree for good, and with it they cannot.
proof.negativeControl: With the old condition, 3 of 3 fail: 'the sender holds claim <older> for the queued attempt, the row carries <newer>: the refresh recorded its own result over the repeat's claim'.

proof.criterion: Both round-17 flakes are gone, and the held-lane order holds through a sweep on the real binary.
proof.surface: internal/dispatch/api under the race detector; two envoy-dispatch processes built from 0433444e on one database
proof.command: GOMAXPROCS=4 CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -p 2 -parallel 4 -race ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^(TestIdenticalViewsShareOneRecompute|TestAHeldLaneKeepsItsQueuedCommentsInOrderThroughASweep)$' -count=50, then the same without -race; steal.sh 45 (listener at 2 s, 45 comments to ses-a)
proof.observed: 50 of 50 each with -race, and 50 of 50 each without. steal.sh: the backlog settles 190 s after the first post, more than three claim leases. ses-a stores c1-c45 once each, in order, and process B sends nothing.
proof.negativeControl: At ed9b6759 each test failed 4 of 20 (round 17).

proof.criterion: The api, events, outbox and store suites pass.
proof.surface: Go suites against Postgres 16 (fresh database t17)
proof.observed: events, outbox and store pass. The api suite's only failure is TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves, which refuses this database's byte-order collation (rank_test.go:317); CI runs it.
proof.negativeControl: None needed for a suite run; the round-17 failures it carried are the control above.
